explanation: Caliph al-Mansur founded Baghdad in 762 as a walled round city. Its scholars translated works by Aristotle, Euclid and Galen, and some later reached Europe through these Arabic versions.

claims.text: The House of Wisdom in Abbasid Baghdad was a centre where Greek works were translated into Arabic.

Caliph al-Mansur founded Baghdad in 762 as a circular walled city.
Works by Aristotle, Euclid and Galen were translated into Arabic in Abbasid Baghdad.
Some Greek works reached medieval Europe through Latin translations of Arabic versions.

issues.note: Some historians (for example Gutas) argue the House of Wisdom was chiefly a library and that the translation movement ran through many patrons across Baghdad. The stem is safe because translators did work in Baghdad, but 'Baghdad's House of Wisdom' is the popular simplification.
